name: Millencolin
label: Epitaph
lede: Three skate rats from Örebro named a band after a trick, signed with a label from their own town and then with Brett Gurewitz's Epitaph. Thirty years on, the four-piece hasn't changed.

eras.title: Skate rats from Örebro
eras.text: Skateboarding and Bad Religion get three friends to start a band in a Swedish city most of the world can't place. By 1994 they have a drummer, two demos and a deal with Burning Heart.

years.src: Wikipedia: Millencolin · Louder: A Short History Of Millencolin
years.h: Skateboarding and Bad Religion start a band in Örebro
years.p: [[Nikola Šarčević|6afaaf35-5be3-4212-8a83-614acff5571b]], Mathias Färm and Erik Ohlsson form Millencolin on October 12, 1992. The name is a spelling twist on the skate trick 'melancholy'.
years.xp:
Louder says the three friends bonded over skateboarding and Bad Religion. Their early influences also included Strung Out, Face To Face, Lagwagon, Pennywise and NOFX.

Wikipedia has Färm on drums at the start, with Šarčević on bass and vocals and Ohlsson on guitar. That lasts until the fourth member turns up.

years.h: Färm hands over the drums and picks up a guitar
years.p: Fredrik Larzon arrives in early 1993 and takes the kit. Färm moves to rhythm guitar, and the four-piece that still plays today is set.

years.src: Louder: A Short History Of Millencolin
years.h: Burning Heart hears the demos and presses a single
years.p: The band records the Goofy demo in early 1993 and Melack in the summer. The Use Your Nose single follows in November on Burning Heart.
years.xp: Burning Heart was an independent label formed in Örebro the same year. Louder says it put out a couple of singles and a covers EP before the debut album.

years.h: Burning Heart puts out Skauch and the debut Tiny Tunes in 1994
years.p: The Skauch EP lands in July, and the album Tiny Tunes follows later the same year, both on Sweden's Burning Heart.

eras.title: Epitaph signs the band from Örebro
eras.text: Ohlsson draws a cover that wins a Swedish prize, and Gurewitz's label takes the record to North America. A Warner Bros. lawsuit over the debut is the decade's one real fight.

years.h: Ohlsson draws the cover for Life on a Plate, and Slitz names it Sweden's best
years.p: Recorded in August 1995 at Unisound in Örebro and out October 11 on Burning Heart, it has a sleeve by guitarist Erik Ohlsson that Slitz magazine picks as Album Cover of the Year.
years.xp:
The album reaches number 4 in Sweden and is later certified gold there, per Wikipedia. Its single 'The Story of My Life' came out in September 1995.

It is the record that gets Epitaph Records interested, and the label releases it in North America in 1996.

years.big: "There's never been a reason not to continue with that relationship."
q: There's never been a reason not to continue with that relationship.
Nikola Šarčević, on staying with Epitaph
years.src: Louder: A Short History Of Millencolin · Wikipedia: Millencolin · Wikipedia: Life on a Plate
years.h: Epitaph takes Life on a Plate across the Atlantic
years.p: Brett Gurewitz's label releases the album on March 26, 1996, and 'Move Your Car' is issued as a single that October.
years.xp:
Šarčević told Louder why the band never left Epitaph: "They know this genre of music better than anyone in the world."

Wikipedia's band page dates Epitaph's first release to late 1995, while the album page says March 26, 1996. This page uses 1996.

years.h: Dan Swanö, known for death metal, engineers For Monkeys
years.p: Recorded in January 1997 at Unisound in Örebro, it brings 'Lozin' Must' and its video. Epitaph releases it in North America on May 20.
years.xp:
It came out in Sweden on April 20 on Burning Heart. Swanö is best known for death and black metal bands.

Šarčević wrote everything except three songs by Mathias Färm: 'Trendy Winds', 'Light's Out' and 'Lowlife'. 'Twenty Two' is the second single, and the album runs 30 minutes 26 seconds.

years.h: Millencolin joins the 1997 Warped Tour
years.p: The American summer circuit puts a band from Örebro in front of skate punk crowds across the US.

years.src: Louder: A Short History Of Millencolin · Wikipedia: Millencolin
years.h: After a Warner Bros. lawsuit, Tiny Tunes becomes Same Old Tunes
years.p: The title and cover art of the debut draw a copyright complaint, and the band re-releases the album in 1998 under the new name.
years.xp: Louder describes it as a copyright infringement lawsuit by Warner Bros. over the title and cover art. Wikipedia calls it legal trouble. The record kept its songs and got a new name.

eras.title: A Hollywood studio and a skateboarding game
eras.text: The band records outside Sweden for the first time, steers away from ska and lands a song on the game every skater is playing.

years.h: Gurewitz produces Pennybridge Pioneers in Hollywood
years.p: Made July to September 1999 at Westbeach with the Epitaph Records boss at the desk, it is the band's first album cut outside Sweden and comes out February 22, 2000.
years.xp:
The record moves away from the band's ska-punk roots toward a more alternative rock sound. The title is a joke: Örebro translates roughly as 'Pennybridge'.

Singles are 'Penguins & Polarbears', 'Fox' and 'No Cigar'. It reached number 13 in Australia and went platinum there by May 2001, per Wikipedia.

years.src: Louder: A Short History Of Millencolin
years.h: 'No Cigar' turns up in Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2
years.p: The single is on the game's soundtrack and comes back in later Tony Hawk remakes.
years.xp: Louder says the song is familiar to anyone who has kickflipped around Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2. The track is from Pennybridge Pioneers, and the game put a band from Örebro in front of a generation of skaters.

years.h: Home from Home reaches number 3 in Australia
years.p: Lou Giordano produced it at Little Big Room in Haninge, September 15 to October 17, 2001. It is out March 12, 2002 in the US.
years.xp:
Europe got it a day earlier on Burning Heart. Singles are 'Kemp', 'Man or Mouse' and 'Battery Check'; the 'Kemp' video was animated by Kalle Haglund, former singer of Voice of a Generation.

On the US tour, Fredrik Larzon injured his elbow and needed surgery in Sweden. Thomas Falk of Bombshell Rocks filled in, and Larzon was back for an Ozzfest date later that year. It also reached number 6 in Sweden.

eras.title: Hometown heroes
eras.text: A Swedish award, a number 2 album and a skatepark of their own turn Millencolin into an Örebro institution.

yt: Full set, Big Day Out, Gold Coast, January 2003
years.h: Sweden hands them the Hit Award for Best Swedish Rock
years.p: A mainstream nod in 2003 for a skate punk band that started in an Örebro rehearsal room.
years.xp: That January, the band played a full set at the Big Day Out in Gold Coast, Australia, a country where Pennybridge Pioneers had already gone platinum and Home from Home reached number 3.

years.cap: Nikola Šarčević live at Conventum, Örebro, April 2008
years.h: Number 2 in Sweden for Kingwood
years.p: Chips Kiesbye produced it, and it's out March 30, 2005 in Sweden. 'Farewell My Hell' began as a Šarčević solo idea.
years.xp:
It was recorded August to October 2004 at Fascination Street and Soundlab in Örebro and Music-A-Matic in Gothenburg. Singles are 'Ray' and 'Shut You Out'; 'Biftek Supernova' went online as a free download on March 1, 2005.

'Farewell My Hell' later turns up in the Swedish vampire comedy Frostbite. The band toured Europe with Street Dogs and The Lawrence Arms in April, played the US West Coast with Boys Night Out and Roses Are Red in May, then the 2005 Warped Tour from mid-June to mid-August. It also reached number 12 in Australia.

years.h: The band runs the Millencolin Open at its own skatepark
years.p: The annual skateboard contest takes place in Örebro, and it ties the music back to the trick behind the band's name.

years.cap: Millencolin on stage in Brazil, October 10, 2008
years.src: Wikipedia: Millencolin · Louder: A Short History Of Millencolin
years.h: After Machine 15, seven years without a studio album
years.p: Recording began October 22, 2007, and the album came out in 2008. The next one, True Brew, arrives in 2015.
years.xp: Sources give the year but not the day. Wikipedia describes the record as high-energy punk rock.

eras.title: Seven quiet years, then a comeback
eras.text: A football song, a two-day birthday festival and two albums keep the original four busy after the long gap.

years.cap: Erik Ohlsson live at Conventum, Örebro, April 2008
years.h: A song for Örebro SK gets its first play at Eyravallen
years.p: The band writes a single called 'Örebro' for the local football club and plays it for the first time at the club's Eyravallen stadium.

years.h: Millencolin throws itself a 20 Year Festival in Örebro
years.p: Two days in June of exclusive sets and international guests mark two decades since October 1992.

years.big: "I can't believe these racist and ignorant views have become normal."
q: I can't believe these racist and ignorant views have become normal and accepted political opinions.
years.src: Louder: A Short History Of Millencolin · Wikipedia: Millencolin
years.h: True Brew ends the long quiet with a record about nationalism
years.p: Released in April 2015, it answers Swedish election debates over nationalism and racism. The band plays Slam Dunk Festival that May.
years.xp:
Louder says the album's lyrics are more overtly political than the band's earlier work, with 'Sense & Sensibility' the clearest case. Šarčević wrote them while the Swedish election debates were pushing nationalism and racism into the mainstream.

It was the band's eighth studio album.

years.cap: Erik Ohlsson and Mathias Färm at Hellfest, France, June 2022
years.h: They record SOS at their own Soundlab studio
years.p: The ninth album comes out on Epitaph on February 15, 2019, recorded at Soundlab in Örebro and mixed by Jens Bogren. It reaches number 15 in Sweden.
